rules.spec_excerpt: DPart hierarchy and page relationships follow ISO 32000-2. Optional Type, RecordLevel and NodeNameList retain prescribed types; a supplied RecordLevel identifies an actual zero-based level. The published Table409 correction prohibits DPart Metadata streams. DPM dictionaries and nested containers contain only permitted value classes, and dictionary keys satisfy the XML name-token constraint. Definite violations fail; unresolved spelling/decoding and bounded traversal remain unavailable. DPartRoot and every DPart node are PDF dictionary objects; a stream with matching entries cannot substitute for one. A leaf requires Start; omitted End defaults to Start for a single-page content set. Single-page leaves omit End.

rules.spec_excerpt: Bind used PDF 2.0 custom EA-PDF tags to the registered EA-PDF namespace and resolve RoleMapNS targets transitively. A name targets the default PDF 1.7 namespace; a two-item array contains a role name and an indirect target namespace dictionary. Resolve to a standard role: Mail_Message to Document, Mail_ContentGroup to Part, Mail_ContentSet to Art, and field tags to appropriate standard roles. Reject malformed targets, unregistered namespaces, cycles and unresolved roles. Reaching an inspection limit leaves the assessment unavailable. Namespace resolution does not replace the separate EA-PDF backward-compatible RoleMap requirements. Standard-only structures continue to omit an unused EA-PDF namespace under the existing local interpretation; section 9.7 does not explicitly state that exemption.

raw_parts:
This section provides a technical description of the EA-PDF v1 file format for readers familiar with the 
technical details of PDF and PDF/A. This section contains requirements that match those described 
in the previous sections. However, many aspects discussed above do not lead to formal 
requirements as they are either covered by existing PDF/A requirements or recommendations, or are 
explanations for EA-PDF developers or end-users.

All “SHALL” mandatory requirements are worded to ensure that they are entirely machine-
validatable. It is assumed that EA-PDF validators do not need to parse any original source raw email 
assets for validation but can parse only PDF data (including content streams) and XMP Metadata to 
perform all validation defined in this document.

Not every PDF feature is listed: if a PDF feature is not mentioned and is not otherwise constrained by 
PDF/A, then it may occur in an EA-PDF file. This applies to many PDF features which do not impact 
the reliable rendering of pages in PDF/A.

Boilerplate and common wording found in PDF ISO subset standards has been intentionally omitted 
from this section so that the focus can be on EA-PDF-specific requirements. Requirements from 
PDF/A are not duplicated here since all EA-PDF files are always conforming PDF/A-3 or PDF/A-4 files.

raw_parts:
For the purposes of EA-PDF validation, a blank PDF page is a page without any visible text, visible 
image, or visible vector as page content or annotations within the page CropBox that would result in 
one or more pixels being painted.
Note: if CropBox is not present, it inherits the value from the MediaBox.
Note: this technical definition for visible is not infallible – a page that marks a single pixel that is white passes this test

but will not normally be visible in a viewing application. It is assumed that all EA-PDF Creation Software is well 
intentioned.
Note: the requirements below are worded such that machine-validation can check consistency between XMP metadata,

PDF content streams, navigation data, and other PDF data structures without referring to the original source email 
assets. This assumes EA-PDF validators can parse both PDF and XMP data, which is not unreasonable for PDF/A 
validators. It is not necessary for a human to perceive the page content to perform EA-PDF validation or to parse 
source email formats.

raw_parts: All PDF/mail-1 files SHALL contain at least one Content Set of at least 1 page each that SHALL NOT
be blank22. The first page in each Content Set in all PDF/mail-1 files SHALL be referenced from at
least one Outline item referenced from the Document Catalog Outlines entry.
Reason: this ensures a basic functional PDF with bookmark (outline) navigation even when the email is empty (e.g., an
empty draft).
Note: the form of the outline destination used is not further defined, while still allowing the page to be validated. This is
also because logical structure is not mandated in EA-PDF.

Each email attachment (as indicated in the document-level XMP metadata) SHALL be visibly 
represented by a File Attachment annotation positioned entirely within the CropBox of a PDF page 
in each Content Set that represents an email body of the source email that contained that 
attachment (as determined by DPM – see below).

Example: if an email has 1 attachment with 2 bodies (HTML and plain text) then there will be at least 2 file attachment

different page (Content Set) associated with the plain text body. There is no requirement that the file attachment 
annotation is always on the first page of the Content Set, although this is conventional. Note that for efficiency both 
annotations could refer to the same file specification dictionary and thus the same embedded file stream. 
Furthermore, both annotations can also share the same appearance stream (e.g., XObject of a paperclip). Additional 
PDF file attachment annotations may also be added by the EA-PDF Creation Software.
Note: this requirement does not constrain how email attachments in other Content Sets (such as an index of email
attachments) might be represented.

raw_parts: When PDF/mail-1{s, m, c} files are directly created from an email source asset (e.g., EML, MSG,

MBOX, NSF, OST/PST, etc.), that exact unmodified asset must also be embedded via the Document 
Catalog AF (Associated Files) array entry in order to create a verifiable preservation asset. This 
results in an Associated Files array element referring to a file specification dictionary with an 
AFRelationship entry of Source (see Table 43, [ISO 32000-2]) and with a Subtype value appropriate 
for Media Type of the original email file format. In non-isolated profiles, there must be at least one 
array element in the Document Catalog where AFRelationship is Source.
Reason: This ensures that the original email file used at EA-PDF creation is always faithfully preserved and clearly

identifiable. Note that AF is always an array (even if there is only a single associated file), even though several PDF 
producers currently generate malformed PDFs using a dictionary!
Note: EA-PDF does not require that only the rendered emails are present in the source email assets. Thus, preserving an
MBOX or PST file with multiple emails in PDF/mail-1s where only a single email is rendered is valid although
potentially inefficient.

7.3.1 Core fields
EA-PDF defines a set of common email header fields and related attributes of each email as Core 
Fields. Each email will have its Core Fields reflected in the document-level XMP of the PDF/mail file

that contains the email. The values used in the XMP must be as equivalent as possible to the full 
value in the source email assets, subject to representation/encoding differences between the source 
email and UTF-8 based XMP.
Reason: as discussed in the LWG, the document level XMP metadata is the primary and definitive source of email

metadata used by document and archival management systems to manage email archives. Core Field names must 
be consistent to enable the most reliable searching across a diverse corpus of EA-PDF files and hence must not be 
localized or vary between EA-PDF Writers. EA-PDF Writers may however localize core fields when it renders this same 
information to PDF page content (e.g., “Subject:” might be rendered as “Objet:” for French emails, but in XMP it will 
always be “Subject” – the value of the field in both cases needs to be the same and not localized).
Note: because the rendering of Core Fields in page content may be truncated, cropped, wrapped, localized, etc., the XMP
Core Fields are to be considered the definitive “source of truth” for all EA-PDF aware software.

formatted email bodies with existing semantic information, PDF logical structure and Tagged PDF is 
strongly recommended.
Reason: Richly formatted emails such as HTML and RTF contain their own semantics, so creation of equivalent PDF data

is possible by EA-PDF Creation Software, but this is not mandated since it cannot be meaningfully validated without 
reference to the original source email data.
Note: it is not mandated that EA-PDF files are also PDF/UA compliant (in addition to the requirement to be PDF/A

compliant) as this imposes additional requirements. However, EA-PDF Creation Software ought to retain an 
equivalent level of semantics of the source email content (e.g., any semantics represented by the HTML tags of HTML 
email bodies ought to be retained when converted to PDF), however determining appropriate semantics from plain 
text emails is implementation dependent.

7.4.2.1 Referenced assets
Subject to the policy environment, EA-PDF Creation Software may additionally decide to preserve 
assets referenced by the original raw source email (e.g., images, SVG, rich media, etc.), including 
fetching and preserving external assets from the internet. When such assets are not natively 
compatible with PDF, the raw asset may also be saved (preserved) in the EA-PDF file as an Associated 
File (in an AF array) to the most relevant PDF object (e.g., Image XObject, Form XObject, font, etc., 
but not the Document Catalog14) with an AFRelationship of Source. See [AssociatedFiles].

The PDF File Attachment annotation must contain a Contents entry and the file specification 
dictionary of the embedded attachment ought to have a meaningful Desc entry. For example, EA-
PDF Creation Software may decide to use these entries to assist in disambiguating email attachments 
for situations where the filename is not unique in an EA-PDF file.
Reason: The Contents key is often used by legacy viewers when navigating file attachment annotations on a PDF page

(such as when hovering over the paperclip icon of the annotation). The embedded file stream dictionary Desc key 
(description) is often used when presenting the list of embedded files in a separate navigation pane. PDF standards 
do not define this level of user experience. Ensuring both are present provides a wider and hopefully more reliable 
legacy viewer experience.

If an attachment exists in the source email but cannot be embedded in the EA-PDF file, then the file 
attachment annotation and embedded file stream representing that attachment ought to be 
created, with the stream Length set to zero bytes.
Reason: this simulates the preserved representation of the email will still appear to have an attachment (via the File

attachment annotation linked to a filename) even in legacy software, even if the bytes of the attachment are 
excluded from preservation (e.g., by a policy setting). However, this is not mandated as it cannot be machine 
validated without referencing the original source email asset.

When the length of the stream data of the embedded file stream is non-zero, the decompressed PDF 
stream data needs to contain the full data of the decompressed email attachment as present in the 
original source email asset.
Note: PDF embedded file streams can be losslessly compressed to reduce PDF file size. PDF does not support Base64 as is
used by email.
Reason: this ensures that the email attachment is faithfully preserved in EA-PDF by not being processed by the EA-PDF

Creation Software which might result in a different bitstream (e.g. line ending changes). However, this is not 
mandated as it cannot be machine validated without referencing the original source email asset.

raw_parts: PDF/mail-1{c, ci} files will always contain one or more pages (in at least one Content Set) that are

used as the initial document. These pages do not represent the content of email but are front matter 
or other content or context related to the entire collection of emails (rather than a single email in the 
collection).
Reason: this ensures that non-EA-PDF aware legacy software does not accidentally present an email from a
PDF/mail-1{c, ci} file in a way that might confuse a user to think that the EA-PDF only contained a single email.

The front matter pages of the container PDF ought to contain content explaining the file is an EA-PDF structured 
container file.

For this reason, the Collection dictionary D entry ([ISO 32000-2], Table 153) must not be present so 
that the page(s) of the PDF/mail-1{c, ci} will be initially shown. These pages may contain one or

more Content Sets at the discretion of the EA-PDF Creation Software. Each Content Set will have 
outline entries (bookmarks) relevant to the content of the container PDF/mail-1{c, ci} file as

described above. As noted in [ISO 32000-2], such pages ought to include information that “… helps 
the user understand what is contained in the collection, such as a title and an introductory paragraph”.
Reason: Content Sets in PDF/mail-1{c, ci} files are left unconstrained and might include content to help users
understand the context of the email collection, conversion reports, policy settings, etc.

Besides the original raw source email asset(s), all the “contained” embedded files in a 
PDF/mail-1{c, ci} must be other EA-PDF files.

the EA-PDF files representing the emails in folders, which might cause confusion when using legacy non-EA-PDF 
aware software.

This section provides a brief discussion on the background and context of the EA-PDF v1.0 file format 
as solicited via the EA-PDF Liaison Working Group (LWG). It does not contain the formal PDF 
technical requirements; however it needs to be read by all users of this document as it explains how 
EA-PDF achieves its goals and the agreed decisions made by the LWG.
Note: this section is descriptive in nature and there are no “SHALL” or “SHOULD” statements. Use of the words “must” or

“will” in this section implies something that is mandated without prescribing exactly how the mandate is technically 
achieved.

raw_parts:
The pages of a sequence of independent document parts are defined in a PDF file using a hierarchy of 
DPart dictionaries referred to as document part dictionaries. The root node of this hierarchy of 
dictionaries is identified by the DPartRoot dictionary referenced from the catalog dictionary. The 
document part hierarchy is a data structure that defines the sequence of pages in the PDF file, 
including any documents and/or document parts of which it is composed. DPart dictionaries that are 
leaf nodes of this hierarchy may refer to a specific range of one or more PDF page objects as identified 
by their Start and End keys. The ranges of PDF page objects referenced from the various DPart 
dictionary leaf nodes shall not overlap and therefore shall not share the same PDF page objects. Each 
page object defined in the PDF file shall be included in the page range defined by one and only one 
DPart dictionary. 
The various DPart dictionary nodes of the hierarchy are fully connected by explicit references to the 
immediate descendant DPart nodes and to the parent node. 
NOTE 1 
Although ISO 32000 also defines structured access to page objects via the pages tree, a PDF 
processor can also access page object entries indirectly from the DPart leaf nodes of the 
document part hierarchy for structured presentation of pages. 
The value of the optional DPartRoot key in the catalog dictionary shall be an indirect object reference 
to a DPartRootNode dictionary. 
A child DPart dictionary shall not be referenced by more than one parent DPart dictionary. 
NOTE 2 
A DPart dictionary is not permitted to have more than one parent and can have any number of 
children because DPart dictionaries are part of a tree structure.

raw_parts: 3.2 EA-PDF Profiles

PDF/mail-1 
Profile

PDF/A 
Conformance 
Levels
Description
PDF/mail-1s
“Single”
PDF/A-3a
PDF/A-3u
PDF/A-4f
PDF/A-4e 3

Single: A single email message preserved as a single EA-
PDF file, where pages in the PDF are a visual 
representation of only that email’s content or context. 
The original raw source email asset(s) are always 
embedded and other files, such as email attachments, 
are also embedded (if present).
Note: this is the basic 1-to-1 verifiable preservation of an email

message as EA-PDF (PDF/A) that non-EA-PDF aware legacy 
software can very reasonably be expected to support.
Note: the embedded original raw email asset may contain

additional emails or other information, but all PDF pages in 
PDF/mail-1s reflect only the single email message.
PDF/mail-1si

“Single, 
isolated”
PDF/A-3a
PDF/A-3u
PDF/A-4
PDF/A-4f
PDF/A-4e

Single, isolated: A single email message preserved as a 
single EA-PDF file, where pages in the PDF are a visual 
representation of the email’s content or context, but the 
original raw source email asset(s) are not embedded (i.e., 
are not faithfully preserved). Other files may be 
embedded (e.g. email attachments).
Note: this is a special EA-PDF profile primarily intended for use in
PDF/mail-1{c, ci} “containers” (see below) or FOIA.
Note: “isolated” means that this class of EA-PDF file is isolated from

its original raw source email asset and thus is not a self-
contained preservation with the associated original raw source 
email assets.

3 PDF/A-4e conformance is only required if 3D or rich media content is required to represent email which is highly 
unlikely. In ISO/DIS 19005-4, PDF/A-4e is formalized as an extension of PDFA-4f.

PDF/mail-1 
Profile

PDF/A 
Conformance 
Levels
Description
PDF/mail-1m
“Multiple”
Note: this is

unrelated to 
the email 
term 
“multipart”.
PDF/A-3a
PDF/A-3u
PDF/A-4f
PDF/A-4fe

Multiple: Multiple emails preserved as a single EA-PDF 
file without folder structure4, where pages in the PDF are 
a visual representation of the content or context of the 
emails. The original raw source email assets are always 
embedded (faithfully preserved).
Note: this is a “flat” preservation of multiple emails. Although non-

EA-PDF aware legacy software will operate with PDF/mail-1m 
files, the level of context available may limit the experience 
(e.g., associating PDF pages with specific emails or email 
attachments, etc.).
Note: a PDF/mail-1m file with only a single email message is

effectively a PDF/mail-1s file. It is required that such files are 
indicated as PDF/mail-1s.
PDF/mail-1mi

“Multiple, 
isolated”
PDF/A-3a
PDF/A-3u
PDF/A-4
PDF/A-4f
PDF/A-4e

Multiple, isolated: Multiple emails preserved as a single 
EA-PDF file without folder structure, where pages in the 
PDF are a visual representation of the content or context 
of the emails. The original raw source email assets are 
not embedded, however other files may be embedded 
(e.g. email attachments).
Note: “isolated” means that this class of EA-PDF file is

disassociated from its original raw source email asset and thus 
is not a self-contained preservation with associated original 
raw source email assets.
Note: this is a special EA-PDF profile primarily intended for use in
PDF/mail-1{c, ci} “containers” (see below).

4 A future version of EA-PDF might consider how to add folder-like structure to PDF/mail-1m files via new PDF 
capabilities. This was not considered at this time as this would not work with any legacy software.

PDF/mail-1 
Profile

PDF/A 
Conformance 
Levels
Description
PDF/mail-1c
“Container”
PDF/A-3a
PDF/A-3u
PDF/A-4f 5

Container: An EA-PDF “structured container” for one or 
more embedded EA-PDF files, each of which may be any 
other PDF/mail-1 profile. PDF/mail-1c files can 
replicate complex folder hierarchies typically found in 
modern email clients, email formats, or file systems. The 
container that is the PDF/mail-1c file does not contain 
pages representing content of preserved emails – all PDF 
representations of email content are in the embedded 
EA-PDF files stored within the container PDF collection. 
Pages in the container PDF represent the context of the 
collection.
Note: there is no requirement that hierarchical folders must be

used, in which case a PDF/mail-1c file is like 
PDF/mail-1m, except that the rendition of emails are 
stored as separate embedded EA-PDF files.
Note: non-EA-PDF aware legacy software needs to support PDF

Collections (PDF 1.7) as otherwise the level of context and

source_selection_policy: Explicit manually selected source blocks and exact physical table rows. No fuzzy matching. Original source spelling and case retained; whitespace reflow only. Merged source values explicitly expanded and recorded.

wording_update.scope: Use the newer user-edited assertions; source quotations, table rows and facsimiles unchanged.

reexamination_decisions.question: Which text controls conflicting requirements?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Use section 9 and its normative tables for file requirements, inherited PDF/PDF-A rules for valid representations, and published errata for corrections. Earlier explanations inform intent; they do not silently strengthen SHOULD into MUST.

reexamination_decisions.question: Can a PDF prove that nothing was lost?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: No. Separate observable internal consistency from source fidelity and creator evidence. Missing or ambiguous evidence must not be reported as a proved match.

reexamination_decisions.question: Which PDF/A-4 edition can be checked now?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Keep the pinned 2020-edition veraPDF profiles as the operational baseline. Equivalence to the cited 2024 draft remains unverified; no duplicate PDF/A engine is invented.

reexamination_decisions.question: Which conformance levels are allowed?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Use the section 9.1 list, including PDF/A-4e, subject to the actual PDF/A feature restrictions. Treat 4fe as the reported spelling error, not a new level.

reexamination_decisions.question: What should a PDF 1.7 collection use for the full-screen exit mode?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Use UseOutlines for PDF 1.7 and UseAttachments for PDF 2.0. Keep the required preference and collection PageMode=UseAttachments. This newly authorized local version exception is not upstream errata.

reexamination_decisions.question: Can sources retained only inside children satisfy the outer collection?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Keep the outer catalog Source requirement as well as independently preserved child sources. The creator retains both; changing preservation ownership needs an author decision.

reexamination_decisions.question: What does an isolated file promise about retained originals?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Isolation does not prohibit retained source files or certify their completeness. Validate supplied asset records and observable links; do not require an invented complete-original inventory for isolated profiles.

reexamination_decisions.question: How should email-to-asset ambiguity be handled?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Keep exact GUID priority and uniquely supported source associations. Report unavailable comparisons when records cannot identify one source; do not add an unstandardized mandatory link property.

reexamination_decisions.question: How should attachment-to-stream ambiguity be handled?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Use independent filename, size, checksum and source evidence within the owning email. Equivalent candidates can prove a field value, not unique identity. Contradiction is proved only when all available candidates disagree.

reexamination_decisions.question: What if Message-ID is duplicated or conflicts with GUID?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Use supplied GUID as the primary identity. Message-ID alone must identify one email. Ambiguity is unavailable evidence; never borrow another message's attachment evidence.

reexamination_decisions.question: Should the missing email Content-Type field be invented?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Preserve the source header and rendered Core Fields where required. Do not invent a mandatory Table 18 property absent from that schema. DPM media-type and attachment Content-Type checks remain separate.

reexamination_decisions.question: Which size/count presence conditions control?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Apply Table 18: SizeInBytes is optional, NumberAttachments is required when there are attachments. Keep source preservation and rendered Core Field obligations separate from XMP property presence.

reexamination_decisions.question: What date should represent an absent or invalid Sent value?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Keep Sent required and correctly typed; retain Raw-Sent when normalization needs it. Never substitute conversion time for an unknown send time. Creation must surface missing required evidence rather than fabricate a valid history.

reexamination_decisions.question: What profile represents an input with no valid messages?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Do not claim s or m conformance for zero messages. Reject an empty email conversion or leave diagnostics outside an EA-PDF claim. A new zero-message profile requires specification clarification.

reexamination_decisions.question: What is the email-list property?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Continue using pdfmailmeta:email as an unordered Bag, as the existing schema interpretation and creator do. Do not introduce a competing property name.

reexamination_decisions.question: Which Message-ID spelling is accepted?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Accept the recorded messageid and Message-ID forms with exact values. If both are supplied they must agree. Keep the creator's canonical output; do not normalize identifier case or punctuation.

reexamination_decisions.question: Is In-Reply-To ordered?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Treat it as an unordered Bag of normal strings. Ordered Seq and Alt do not satisfy this local interpretation.

reexamination_decisions.question: How should addresses and malformed originals be represented?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Use ordered FOAF Agent records and supported equivalent URI/text forms. Preserve non-SMTP or malformed originals in raw fields rather than fabricate mailboxes. Unhandled legal representations remain unavailable.

reexamination_decisions.question: Must the attachments Bag always exist?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Yes, including an empty Bag. Complete original attachment inventory remains SHOULD. Required property presence and required supplied-record schema are distinct from recommended completeness.

reexamination_decisions.question: Can malformed original media types be silently repaired?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: No. Preserve original metadata text, use a valid embedded-stream media type, and report a real disagreement or unavailable comparison honestly. Where both printed demands cannot be met, do not fabricate conformance or invent a second mandatory raw-type property.

reexamination_decisions.question: Should reconstruction add an empty trailing semicolon?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Append the separator only for nonempty parameters. Absent and empty parameter text add no semicolon; a supplied non-text value still fails its type check.

reexamination_decisions.question: Must there be exactly one source?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Require at least one source for nonisolated preservation profiles; permit multiple independent sources. The contradictory word only does not impose a universal maximum.

reexamination_decisions.question: Is the catalog key Collection or Collections?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Use the defined PDF Collection key. Retain the source spelling error as a question for the authors.

reexamination_decisions.question: What does the collection Size column measure?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Keep the required Size subtype and interpret it as embedded PDF bytes. Original email bytes belong in email XMP; do not replace the required field with N.

reexamination_decisions.question: Which minimum collection schema applies?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Use Table 6, including Message-ID, together with compatible Table 5 requirements. Keep Bcc; missing source identifiers or recipients must not be fabricated.

reexamination_decisions.question: How should a collection summarize a child containing many emails?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Require the schema, not an invented first-message summary. The current creator emits single-message children. Validators permit absent item values where PDF allows them; aggregation semantics remain an author question.

reexamination_decisions.question: Which tag replaces the undefined Mail_ContentField?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Retain the already approved Mail_Field interpretation and the immediate-child checks.

reexamination_decisions.question: Where do collection content sets belong?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Under the outer Document, with no Mail_Message. Keep the collection exception and the separate prohibition on email content in collection front matter.

reexamination_decisions.question: Where do archive-wide front matter and reports belong?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: At document level in both DPart and logical structure. For noncollections, the ancestry exception requires verified content connections to document-wide FrontMatter, ConversionReport or PolicySettings with no email identity in their DPart ancestry. A tag attribute alone cannot select the exception.

reexamination_decisions.question: When do custom-tag rules apply?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Apply custom vocabulary rules only when that vocabulary is used. Preserve inherited tagging requirements for the selected PDF/A level. Standard-only tagged PDF 2.0 still requires ISO/TS 32005.

reexamination_decisions.question: Must unused tags be mapped and must standard tags use the EA namespace?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Require Table 9 mappings for tags actually used. Require the EA namespace for custom EA tags; keep RoleMap and RoleMapNS distinct and Artifact-to-Private direction. No guarantee of lossless PDF 1.7 interpretation of all PDF 2.0 namespaces is claimed.

reexamination_decisions.question: What XMP field matches ContentGroup ContentSetType?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: None is defined. Compare the supplied attribute with its actual DPart content; leave the unnamed XMP comparison explicitly unverified. Do not invent metadata to make the comparison appear complete.

reexamination_decisions.question: Does blankness apply per page or per set?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Each declared set must contain at least one nonblank page. Other pages may be blank. Keep this existing runtime interpretation and correct the descriptions; page count, range validity and visible content are separate checks.

reexamination_decisions.question: Where must attachments be exposed without a BodyRendering set?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: The stated per-body annotation obligation is not applicable when absence of all body sets is known. The creator continues to provide attachment notices/lists. No universal fallback location is invented as a mandatory validator rule.

reexamination_decisions.question: Is preservation of all original text mandatory?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Rendered Core Fields must use text objects; full source-text representation is SHOULD under section 9. Preserve that distinction in rule summaries and reports.

reexamination_decisions.question: May Figure 6 identifiers replace the normative schema?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: No. Keep the Table 14 namespaces and Table 15 version property. The faulty diagram remains source-maintenance work.

reexamination_decisions.question: May example errors define media parameters or object syntax?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: No. Use valid MIME parameter syntax and actual PDF object types. Keep example corrections as questions for the source authors; preserve the pinned publication unchanged.

reexamination_decisions.question: Which collection ownership example controls?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Use the explicit ownership requirements and valid PDF object references, not the swapped left/right prose or duplicate sample object number.

reexamination_decisions.question: Should the sample DPart tree be copied literally?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: No. Keep valid parent/child/page relationships, prohibit DPart Metadata under the published correction, and retain source diagrams as evidence of the errors.

reexamination_decisions.question: Should Example 7 override the tag tables?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: No. Use Mail_ContentSet for sets, valid TJ array operands, permitted root array form and explicit namespace connections. Existing creator and validators enforce these independently of the faulty example.

reexamination_decisions.question: Which attachment-set review answer is current?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: The mandatory empty-or-populated Bag decision supersedes the old omission allowance. Update the active question, inventory and generated views while retaining dated history as superseded.

reexamination_decisions.question: What does an individual rule PASS establish?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Only the check named in that rule: presence, type, allowed value, page range, visible content or a specific comparison. Update descriptions that previously claimed the entire combined requirement.

reexamination_decisions.question: Should recommendations sound mandatory in standalone text?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: No. Use should explicitly for recommendations and must for mandatory supplied-value conditions. Preserve the separate strength metadata.

reexamination_decisions.question: Where should implementation history and local assumptions live?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Keep concise current requirements in runtime JSON. Retain previous detailed text in the separate review JSON and record current assumptions here; do not lose evidence by deleting the history.

reexamination_decisions.question: Does mapping every requirement prove execution?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: No. NumberMessages currently proves integer type, not the number rendered from each source. The body media comparator does not prove AttachmentRendering source fidelity. Keep these limits explicit; dependable source-to-rendering associations remain necessary and are not invented.

reexamination_decisions.question: Which documents and counts are current?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Runtime JSON has 213 rules; separate review JSON holds 301 inventory records. Regenerate current views from both. Label older counts and acceptance results as historical.

reexamination_decisions.question: How are creator-only preservation duties evidenced?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Link inventory duties to creator coverage review and relevant source-fidelity/creator tests. These links provide bounded evidence, not a new claim of exhaustive preservation for unsupported original formats.

reexamination_decisions.question: Which creation event does CreateDate record?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: The EA-PDF creation event. Preserve original dates separately. Both validators distinguish a valid date value from unavailable provenance, and cannot prove history merely by comparing Sent.

reexamination_decisions.question: Should the malformed source PDF be repaired in place?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: No. Preserve its pinned bytes and hash, document the invalid number trees, and request a corrected publication upstream when authorized. It is not a known-valid test PDF.

reexamination_decisions.question: Can the two metadata schemas share normalized field names?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: No. Preserve asset ContentType/Checksum and attachment Content-Type/CheckSum exactly. Do not introduce aliases based on the upstream complaint.

reexamination_decisions.question: May preserved malformed HTML bypass ISO/TS 32005?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: No. Repair structure where possible while preserving source bytes and recording conversion limits. Tagged PDF 2.0 must still meet the published requirement; optional PDF/UA is not imposed.

reexamination_decisions.question: Which supporting guidance overrides old examples?
reexamination_decisions.assumption: Apply published inherited corrections, including DPM names and MCAF. Keep known edition/schema guidance gaps visible; issue proposals and reported EC3 publication fixes do not silently replace pinned documents.
